claims.statement: The operations module is the presentation-free business-logic boundary shared by CLI, TUI, and MCP: its functions take an HteamClient (and Config when persistence is needed) and return domain data, while delivery surfaces choose presentation.

The configured board number and the API board_id are distinct identifiers: the number selects board-scoped list/task routes, while the API board_id is extracted from card-list entries and is required for create-card and card-label routes.

Resolving an uncached API board_id first inspects cards in list 1, then nonempty lists when Open is empty; failure to find a card-list entry produces an error, and setting a new board number clears the cached API board_id.
Switching the active board persists its number to config.toml and ~/.last_ticket, updates stored board display metadata, and records a last-used timestamp.

A card-list response wraps Cards in CardListEntry records that separately carry a list-entry ID, API board_id, closure/type/time/position metadata; list_cards returns nested cards plus only the first entry's board_id.
CardDetail is the richer read/edit task shape, and its label deserializer accepts arrays of label objects while converting scalar or incompatible label payloads to an empty label vector.

The move-card request sends the card id, source and destination list ids, card_type: 0, and the selected board number in board_id; callers must supply the source list because the client does not infer it inside move_card.

Creating a card resolves API board_id, active board number, and user ID, posts process/complement/labels values, and can return an id-0 placeholder after a successful response when an empty or unusable response cannot be reconciled by exact name lookup in the requested list.

Card updates are read-modify-write: update_card fetches CardDetail before update_card_full posts the complete edit form, preserving unspecified fields from the detail and defaulting absent priority to 3.

Posting a comment first fetches the board-specific task page to extract timestamp, security_hash, and CSRF form values; it posts a form for processes.task with reply_to 0, sends follow only when true, and rejects HTTP status 400 or higher.
Reminder creation posts a fixed reminder payload with type 1, object_id set to the card id, and card_type 0, and it treats HTTP status 400 or higher as an error.

WorkingOnStatus.id is a working-on-it record ID while card_id is the remote object_id; starting work takes the card ID, but stopping work requires the working-record ID and sends state 4 with content type 99.

Working-on-it reads normalize empty/null, array, and singleton endpoint responses; authenticated user-ID discovery uses a working record first, falls back to the last work-shift user, and persists a resolved user ID.

Project milestones deserialize from positional name/progress/url tuples, project tasks include optional milestone and responsible references, and remembering a project deduplicates it, moves it to the front of tui.known_projects, and saves config.
The MCP server exposes board/card, comment, reminder, working, project, user, and check-in operations through the shared operations boundary and maps operation errors to MCP internal errors.

The board and card layer is presentation-free domain logic: `operations` exposes data and mutations to CLI, TUI, and MCP, while `HteamClient` owns the authenticated HTTP workflow; local configuration stores active board number, cached internal `board_id`, known boards, and user ID, but not board contents.

Operation/process numbers, internal `board_id` values, list IDs, card IDs, card-list entry IDs, working-on-it record IDs, and other endpoint-specific IDs are distinct and must be used in the right routes; `CardListEntry` carries the internal `board_id` while `Card` and `CardDetail` carry the task identity.

Hteam keeps operation tasks and project tasks on separate API trees, and `TaskFamily` is inferred from `title_url` so project card detail and edit flows can use `/projects/{id}/tasks/{task_id}/` instead of the configured operation board.

When the client needs an internal `board_id`, it first checks cached configuration, then inspects list `1` (Open) and takes the first card-list entry's `board_id`; if Open is empty it falls back to other nonempty lists, and if nothing yields a board id it fails with `No se pudo obtener board_id`.

`List` carries an ID, name, and optional card count, while `CardListResponse` wraps cards in `CardListEntry` records that include wrapper identity, `board_id`, closure, type, time, and position metadata; `get_cards_for` returns the nested cards plus only the first entry's `board_id`, discarding the wrapper metadata after extraction.

`Card` maps the API's `title`, `subtitle`, and `labels_list` fields to Rust `name`, optional `description`, and labels, while `CardDetail` is the richer read/edit shape that retains status, list, timestamps, estimate, start date, dependency, responsible, priority, close state, milestone, and `title_url`.

Label decoding for `CardDetail` is intentionally defensive: the deserializer keeps only successfully parsed label objects and turns scalar or incompatible payloads into an empty label list, so malformed label payloads do not break detail reads.

`card_detail_enriched` reconstructs editing state from three sources: task detail JSON, board-card JSON, and the HTML edit form baseline; for project tasks it resolves the project board id and form path from `title_url`, then merges board-card fields and finally fills remaining gaps from the edit form.

The board-card merge rules prefer board-card values for estimated time, spent time, date fields, labels, responsible, and missing priority when those fields are available, but only replace existing data when the incoming value is meaningful; the edit-form merge then supplies priority and time estimate only when they are still missing.

Safe card edits are read-modify-write: `update_card_full` fetches the HTML edit form before posting the complete form body back, and the merge logic preserves sibling fields by using the form baseline instead of rebuilding the request from task JSON alone.

Card creation requires the internal `board_id`, active board number, and user ID; it POSTs `process` as the board number, `complement` as the user ID, and `labels` as an empty array or a single supplied `list_id`, and if the created card cannot be recovered it falls back to a placeholder card with `id: 0`.

Moving a card posts the card id, source and destination list ids, `card_type: 0`, and the selected board number under `board_id`; the convenience wrapper defaults an omitted source list to `1` (Open), so callers should pass `from_list` when the card might be elsewhere.
The client exposes `open_cards` and `closed_cards` as convenience wrappers over list ids `1` and `2`; that Open/Closed convention is client-side convenience rather than a remote schema guarantee.

Using the wrong identifier or family can corrupt board state: card-specific endpoints expect card ids, board-card AJAX routes expect the internal `board_id`, and operation and project URLs must match the task family encoded in `title_url`.

`Card::has_follow_up` detects the special Follow-up label by name, and `get_cards_for` copies `CardListEntry.get_time_status` into `Card.time_status` only for cards that carry that label so the UI does not show irrelevant follow-up metadata on ordinary cards.
`priority_label` normalizes Hteam priority values into human-readable labels, accepting either numeric or string inputs and mapping 1 through 5 to the localized labels used by the CLI and TUI.

The card search API applies AND semantics across filters: text is matched case-insensitively against name and description, labels require every requested label name to match some card label by case-insensitive equality, and responsible/priority are compared against the display text extracted from the payload.
The search scope carries an optional board, optional list filter, and a TaskFamily so the same search code can target either operation or project board trees.

The TUI uses `Card::has_follow_up` to decide whether to fetch follow-up details for the selected card, which keeps follow-up lookups aligned with the board-layer label convention rather than with a separate card flag.
